hints.title: Subtree Swapping Obstacle
hints.text: Inverting a tree requires swapping left and right subtrees at every level. If you swap the children of a node first, what happens to their unvisited child subtrees? How can recursive subproblem decomposition ensure every descendant is inverted?

hints.title: Mirror Inversion Invariant
hints.text: The inverse of a binary tree is formed by swapping its left and right subtrees, where each subtree is itself recursively inverted.

hints.title: Recursive Pointer Swap Procedure
hints.text: Base case: if the current node is null, return null. Swap the node's left and right child pointers. Recursively call the inversion procedure on the left child and right child. Return the current node.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 100)
H: height of tree (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Every node is visited once and swapped in-place. Auxiliary space is bounded by the recursion stack height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rebuilding a new mirrored tree from serialization requires extra node allocations and multiple passes taking O(N) space and higher overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place pointer swapping achieves O(N) time with O(H) call stack frames without allocating new nodes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear base case for null root, in-place child pointer swap, understanding recursion stack space proportional to height.
